headline: Language models are benchmarked on biological tasks from variant ranking to GO clustering
label: Llm Benchmarks For Biology
summary: Preprints and a publication test whether general LLMs and embeddings can support protein variant ranking and gene-set hypothesis testing.
synthesis: The common thread is rigorous evaluation of language-model outputs against biological ground truth rather than model construction. PG-LLM benchmarks 13 general-purpose LLMs and 95 published predictors on 276 protein-variant ranking tasks, with top LLMs reaching Spearman ~0.41. The embedding-based framework treats LLM-inferred gene-set functions as hypotheses to be tested statistically, benchmarking seven embedding models on GO processes and pathways. LLMBDC applies training-free zero-shot reasoning with confidence scoring to group GO enrichment terms into biological domains. GraphRareBench adds an auditable angle, providing 2,365 phenotype cases with hard confounders and provenance-preserving evidence records for rare-disease diagnosis. The items are heterogeneous, and only PG-LLM concerns protein sequence directly. What is new is emphasis on calibrated, provenance-aware assessment of general-purpose models in biology.
